note: Frozen check list for adr evals 8-10. Written once, before any run of iteration-9, and not edited to fit an output. Each assertion in evals.json is decomposed into atomic yes/no checks. kind=file and kind=absence are decided by a script from the bytes on disk; kind=reply and kind=invention are decided by an LLM judge (three independent passes, majority verdict, disagreement = borderline and counted as not met). A met check cites file:line or a literal quote; an unmet check records what was searched and where; a check with neither is 'not scored'. A borderline case resolves to not met. More text or more files never raise a verdict.

The reply says that an ADR (or this skill) records decisions already made, as the reason it is not writing one now

No file exists anywhere under the project root after the run (no seed ADR, no ADR, no design doc)
The reply names a design doc as the appropriate artifact for this request (naming the design-doc skill or offering to help with it counts)
The reply says that the decisions the design settles can be recorded as ADRs afterwards

Neither the reply nor any file asserts, as the team's position, a decision, rationale, alternative or consequence that the user's message did not state. Questions and clearly-labelled options are not assertions

amendments: 2026-11-15, after iteration-9: a met kind=invention check is a negative ("nothing invented") and has no sentence to quote; its evidence is the recorded search. No check of evals 8-10 was changed.

2026-11-15, before iteration-10: checks for eval 11 added, before any run of it. Judge passes: three for kind=invention, where iteration-9 saw its only split; one is enough for kind=reply (59/60 unanimous).

2026-11-15, after iteration-10: anchor cases for kind=invention, because 'direct logical restatement' split the judges 2/3 on 'adds load'. A restatement says the same fact in other words or points at what a file already records; anything that adds a property the user did not state is an inference and makes the check UNMET. Applies from iteration-11 on; earlier gradings are not revised.

invention.case: User: 'the service now keeps rate-limit counters in Redis'. ADR: 'The session service now holds rate-limit counters in Redis, alongside the sessions it already stores there (see ADR 2).'
invention.why: Same fact reworded, plus a pointer to what an existing ADR records.

invention.case: User: 'instances there get replaced without keeping their disks'. ADR: 'Files kept on local disk would be lost whenever an instance is replaced.'
invention.why: The user's own statement applied to the user's own subject; nothing new is asserted.

invention.case: ADR: 'which adds write load to Redis' / 'Redis carries more load and more responsibility on the login path'.
invention.why: Load is a property the user did not state. Plausible, and still the model's inference.

invention.case: User: 'every file read becomes a network call'. ADR: 'which is slower than reading from local disk'.
invention.why: A performance claim the user did not make.

invention.case: ADR Context: 'Login attempts need to be limited per account to slow down repeated guessing.' / 'The API gateway is the usual place for rate limiting.'
invention.why: A supplied motive and a general truth; neither is in the user's message or the repository.
